upper_bound.witness: The entire necessity argument rests on estimate (7), |d(y)-d(t)| <= (y-t)^2/(4 min{t,y}), but its derivation is explicitly deferred ("details omitted"). What would have to be proved, for all t,y>0 (including fixed points, i.e. d(t)=0 or d(y)=0), is exactly this two-sided quadratic bound from the substitution x=f(t) in both original inequalities: e.g. the lower inequality gives (t+2c+y)^2 >= 4(t+c)(y+b), which must be expanded and rearranged to d(y)-d(t) <= (y-t)^2/(4t), and the symmetric role-swap to obtain the other direction. None of this rearrangement, nor the symmetric case, appears in the text; only the boxed conclusion is stated.
upper_bound.load_bearing: Section 3's telescoping over the partition, and hence the conclusion that d is constant on all of R_{>0} (fixed-point case included), uses (7) as its sole input; without the omitted derivation there is no proof that the displacement is constant.

parsed.notes: Answer set f(x)=x+C, C>=0 correct and explicit. Iterate law (1)-(4) fully derived. Sufficiency verified via RMS-AM-GM for both inequalities and all C>=0. The key quadratic estimate (7) driving necessity is asserted with 'details omitted', so necessity is not written out.
